'''Dalton Douglas Knecht''' ({{IPAc-en|k|ə|'|n|ɛ|k|t}}; born April 19, 2001) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for [[Northeastern Junior College]], [[Northern Colorado Bears men's basketball|Northern Colorado]], and [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee]]. He was selected 17th overall by the Lakers in the [[2024 NBA draft]].

==Early life==
Knecht is the son of Corey and Carrie Knecht.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dalton Knecht - Men's Basketball |url=https://utsports.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/dalton-knecht/19129 |website=University of Tennessee Athletics |access-date=July 26, 2024 |language=en}}</ref> Knecht was born in [[Fargo, North Dakota]], and grew up in [[Thornton, Colorado]], attending Prairie View High School in [[Henderson, Colorado|Henderson]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowlin |first=Ryan |date=June 27, 2024 |title=#NDProud: Fargo Born Dalton Knecht Drafted No. 17 by LA Lakers |url=https://www.kvrr.com/2024/06/27/ndproud-fargo-born-dalton-knecht-drafted-no-17-by-la-lakers/ |access-date=June 29, 2024 |website=KVRR Local News |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.9news.com/article/sports/ncaa/ncaab/dalton-knecht-helping-lead-northern-colorado-basketball/73-53876faa-0521-4477-ada1-62f87c093342|title=Colorado native Dalton Knecht helping lead UNC basketball|first=Jacob|last=Tobey|website=[[9news.com]]|date=January 28, 2023|access-date=November 11, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Peterson |first=Eric |date=June 27, 2024 |title=PHOTOS: Tennessee's Dalton Knecht set to join LeBron in LA as Enderlin celebrates |url=https://www.jamestownsun.com/sports/pro/photos-tennessees-dalton-knecht-set-to-join-lebron-in-la-as-enderlin-celebrates |access-date=June 29, 2024 |website=Jamestown Sun |language=en}}</ref> He entered his sophomore year at {{Height|ft=5|in=8|abbr=mos}} and grew to {{Height|ft=6|in=1|abbr=mos}} by his junior year.<ref name=rtt>{{cite web|url=https://www.rockytoptalk.com/2023/4/21/23693543/northern-colorado-transfer-dalton-knecht-commits-to-tennessee-vols-basketball|title=Northern Colorado transfer Dalton Knecht commits to Tennessee|first=Terry A.|last=Lambert|website=RockyTopTalk.com|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|date=April 21, 2023|access-date=November 11, 2023}}</ref> Knecht averaged 21 points and 6.5 rebounds per game as a senior.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Watson-Fisher |first=Jadyn |date=November 12, 2020 |title=Northern Colorado athletic programs add 20 signees to 2021 rosters |url=https://www.fortmorgantimes.com/2020/11/12/university-northern-colorado-adds-20-freshmen-2021/ |access-date=November 11, 2023 |website=[[The Fort Morgan Times]]}}</ref>

==College career==
Knecht began his college basketball career at [[Northeastern Junior College]] in [[Sterling, Colorado]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dalton Knecht |url=https://www.gonjc.com/sports/mbkb/2020-21/bios/knecht_dalton_53ud |access-date=June 28, 2024 |website=Northeastern Junior College |language=en}}</ref> He grew another two inches between his senior high school season and his first season with the Plainsmen.<ref name=rtt/> Knecht averaged 13.3 points, 2.9 rebounds and 1.1 assists per game as a freshman.<ref name="commitnc">{{Cite web |last=Pisani |first=Hart |date=November 12, 2020 |title=NJC's Dalton Knecht signs with UNC Bears |url=https://www.journal-advocate.com/2020/11/12/njcs-dalton-knecht-signs-with-unc-bears/ |access-date=November 11, 2023 |website=[[Journal-Advocate]]}}</ref> He averaged 23.9 points, 7.5 rebounds and two assists per game as a sophomore.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.on3.com/teams/tennessee-volunteers/news/tennessee-vols-basketball-dalton-knecht-scorer-shoot-feel-good-going-in/|title=In Italy Dalton Knecht showed why when he shoots 'you feel good about it going in'|first=Grant|last=Ramey|website=On3.com|date=August 9, 2023|access-date=November 11, 2023}}</ref> Knecht grew another three inches during his time playing at Northeastern Junior College to bring his height to {{Height|ft=6|in=6|abbr=mos}}.<ref name=rtt/> He committed to transfer to [[Northern Colorado Bears men's basketball|Northern Colorado]] to continue his college career.<ref name=commitnc/>

Knecht averaged 8.9 points and 3.6 rebounds per game in his first season with the Northern Colorado Bears.<ref>{{cite web |last=Ankony |first=Jack |date=April 5, 2023 |title=Indiana To Meet With Northern Colorado Transfer Dalton Knecht |url=https://www.si.com/college/indiana/basketball/indiana-basketball-to-meet-with-northern-colorado-transfer-dalton-knecht |access-date=November 11, 2023 |website=[[SI.com]]}}</ref> As a senior, he led the [[Big Sky Conference]] with 20.2 points and 7.2 rebounds per game.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Watson-Fisher |first=Jadyn |date=March 14, 2023 |title=Dalton Knecht becomes fourth Bear to earn NABC All-District honors |url=https://www.greeleytribune.com/2023/03/14/dalton-knecht-northern-colorado-basketball-nabc-all-district-team/ |access-date=November 11, 2023 |website=[[Greeley Tribune]]}}</ref> After the season, Knecht decided to utilize the extra year of eligibility granted to college athletes who played in the [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2020–21 season]] due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]] and entered the [[NCAA transfer portal]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Watson-Fisher |first=Jadyn |date=March 23, 2023 |title=Northern Colorado men's basketball: Dalton Knecht enters transfer portal |url=https://www.greeleytribune.com/2023/03/23/northern-colorado-basketball-dalton-knecht-transfer-portal/ |access-date=November 11, 2023 |website=[[Greeley Tribune]]}}</ref>

Knecht transferred to [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee]] for the [[2023–24 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2023–24 season]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Moore |first1=CJ |last2=Vecenie |first2=Sam |date=April 21, 2023 |title=Former Northern Colorado guard Dalton Knecht transfers to Tennessee |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4438439/2023/04/21/northern-colorado-dalton-knecht-tennessee/ |access-date=November 11, 2023 |website=[[The Athletic]] |via=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=November 11, 2023 |title=Dalton Knecht offers what Tennessee basketball has been missing |url=https://www.knoxnews.com/story/sports/college/university-of-tennessee/mens-basketball/2023/11/11/dalton-knecht-tennessee-basketball-wisconsin-score-rick-barnes-santiago-vescovi-zakai-zeigler/71321174007/ |url-access=subscription |access-date=November 11, 2023 |work=[[Knoxville News Sentinel]]}}</ref> He was named the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) Player of the Week for the first week of the season after scoring 17 points in the Volunteers' season-opening win over [[2023–24 Tennessee Tech Golden Eagles men's basketball team|Tennessee Tech]] and 24 points with five rebounds in an 80–70 road victory over [[2023–24 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team|Wisconsin]] on November 10, 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/tennessee/mens-basketball/dalton-knecht-sec-player-of-the-week|title=Dalton Knecht Named SEC Player Of The Week|first=Jonathan|last=Lidskin|website=[[SI.com]]|date=November 14, 2023|access-date=November 17, 2023}}</ref> Knecht scored a then-career-high 37 points in a 100–92 loss to [[2023–24 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]] on November 29, 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Paschall |first=David |date=November 29, 2023 |title=Knecht's 37 points not enough as Vols fall at North Carolina |url=https://www.timesfreepress.com/news/2023/nov/29/knechts-37-points-not-enough-as-vols-fall-at/ |access-date=December 15, 2023 |website=[[Chattanooga Times Free Press]]}}</ref> He was named the SEC Player of the Week a second time on January 15, 2024, after scoring 28 points in a 77–72 loss to [[2023–24 Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball team|Mississippi State]] and 36 points in an 85–79 win over [[2023–24 Georgia Bulldogs basketball team|Georgia]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Taylor |first=Noah |date=January 15, 2024 |title=Vols' guard Dalton Knecht named Co-SEC Player of the Week |url=https://tennessee.rivals.com/news/vols-guard-dalton-knecht-named-co-sec-player-of-the-week |access-date=January 17, 2024 |website=[[Rivals.com]]}}</ref> Knecht set a then career high with 39 points in an 85–66 win over [[2023–24 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]] on January 16, 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wilson |first=Mike |date=January 16, 2024 |title=Dalton Knecht scorches Florida as Tennessee basketball rolls Gators |url=https://www.knoxnews.com/story/sports/college/university-of-tennessee/mens-basketball/2024/01/16/tennessee-basketball-score-florida-dalton-knecht/72121121007/ |access-date=March 8, 2024 |website=Knoxville News Sentinel |language=en-US}}</ref> On February 29, 2024, Knecht tied his then-career high with 39 points against 11th-ranked [[2023–24 Auburn Tigers men's basketball team|Auburn]] in a 92–84 win.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Auburn Tigers vs. Tennessee Volunteers Live Score and Stats - February 28, 2024 Gametracker |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/gametracker/live/NCAAB_20240228_AUBURN@TENN/ |access-date=March 6, 2024 |website=CBS Sports |language=en}}</ref> On March 9, 2024, Knecht set a new career high on senior night with 40 points in an 85–81 loss to 15th-ranked [[2023–24 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rexrode |first=Joe |date=March 10, 2024 |title=Vols' loss to Kentucky despite Dalton Knecht's 40 makes SEC tournament mission clear |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5329162/2024/03/10/tennessee-vols-kentucky-dalton-knecht-sec-tournament/ |access-date=June 28, 2024 |website=The New York Times |language=en-US}}</ref>

Knecht was named [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|SEC Player of the Year]] by both the league's coaches<ref name=SECCoachesAwards>{{cite press release |url=https://www.secsports.com/news/2024/03/2024-sec-mens-basketball-awards-announced |title=2024 SEC Men's Basketball Awards announced |publisher=Southeastern Conference |date=March 11, 2024 |access-date=March 11, 2024}}</ref> and the [[Associated Press]] (AP).<ref name=SECAPAwards>{{cite news |url=https://apnews.com/article/all-sec-team-a64c6f42fd83f4dfb4b3cebec5902000 |title=Tennessee's Dalton Knecht named AP's SEC player of year; South Carolina's Paris is coach of year |first=John |last=Zenor |agency=Associated Press |date=March 12, 2024 |access-date=March 12, 2024}}</ref> He was also named [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year|SEC Newcomer of the Year]] by the AP.<ref name=SECAPAwards/>{{efn|The Newcomer of the Year award is one of two awards presented to the top player in his first season of SEC play. The league's coaches vote on a Freshman of the Year award, restricted to players in their first season playing college basketball; this award went to [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]]'s [[Reed Sheppard]] in 2024.<ref name=SECCoachesAwards/>}}

==Professional career==
=== Los Angeles Lakers (2024–present) ===
Knecht was selected with the 17th overall pick by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in the [[2024 NBA draft]]<ref>{{cite web |last=McMenamin |first=Dave |date=June 27, 2024 |title=Lakers thrilled with Dalton Knecht pick: 'Extraordinary' value |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/40441805 |access-date=June 27, 2024 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> and he signed with them on July 3, 2024.<ref>{{cite web |date=July 3, 2024 |title=Los Angeles Lakers Sign Dalton Knecht and Bronny James |url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/los-angeles-lakers-sign-dalton-knecht-and-bronny-james-070324 |access-date=July 3, 2024 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

Knecht made his NBA debut on October 22, 2024, in a 110–103 win over the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], scoring 5 points.<ref>{{cite web |date=October 26, 2024 |title=Minnesota Timberwolves at Los Angeles Lakers Box Score, October 22, 2024 |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202410220LAL.html |access-date=October 26, 2024 |website=Basketball-Reference.com}}</ref> On November 13, Knecht scored a then career-high 19 points on 7-of-8 shooting from the field with 5-of-5 shooting from three-point range in a 128–123 win over the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Gomez |first=Michael Aaron |date=November 14, 2024 |title=JJ Redick shouts out true 'catalyst' for Lakers' comeback win vs. Grizzlies |url=https://clutchpoints.com/lakers-news-jj-redick-shouts-out-true-catalyst-comeback-win-grizzlies |access-date=November 14, 2024 |website=ClutchPoints}}</ref> Three days later, he broke this record, scoring a then career-high 27 points along with seven rebounds, two assists, and two steals in a 104–99 win over the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/lakers-news-dalton-knecht-new-career-high-3-quarters-pelicans|title=Dalton Knecht sets new career-high in just 3 quarters vs. Pelicans|website=ClutchPoints|last=Yapkowitz|first=David|date=November 16, 2024|access-date=November 16, 2024}}</ref> On November 19, Knecht scored a career-high 37 points, including nine three-pointers, in a 124–118 victory against the [[Utah Jazz]]. He also tied the record for the most three-pointers made in a single game by a rookie in NBA history.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Woike |first=Dan |date=November 19, 2024 |title=Red-hot Dalton Knecht scores 37 points as Lakers win sixth in a row |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/lakers/story/2024-11-19/los-angeles-lakers-utah-jazz-nba-dalton-knecht |access-date=November 20, 2024 |work=[[Los Angeles Times]]}}</ref>

On February 6, 2025, the Lakers agreed to trade Knecht, [[Cam Reddish]], a future first-round pick, and a pick swap to the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in exchange for [[Mark Williams (basketball)|Mark Williams]].<ref>{{cite web |date=February 6, 2025 |title=Los Angeles Lakers Acquire Center Mark Williams |url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/los-angeles-lakers-acquire-center-mark-williams-02062025 |website=NBA.com |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250207062711/https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/los-angeles-lakers-acquire-center-mark-williams-02062025 |archive-date=February 7, 2025 |url-status=dead }}</ref> However, the trade was rescinded two days later after Williams failed his physical with the Lakers.<ref>{{cite web |last=McDaniel |first=Mike |date=February 8, 2025 |title=Trade Sending Mark Williams to Lakers, Dalton Knecht to Hornets Rescinded |url=https://www.si.com/nba/trade-sending-mark-williams-to-lakers-dalton-knecht-to-hornets-rescinded |access-date=February 8, 2025 |website=Sports Illustrated}}</ref>  Returning to the Lakers, for the rest of February, he scored 5.1 points per game and shot 32.1% on three-point shots.<ref name="gamelog">{{cite web |title=Dalton Knecht 2024-25 Stats per Game - NBA |url=https://www.espn.com.sg/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4897943/type/nba/year/2025 |website=ESPN |access-date=1 November 2025}}</ref>  However, during March and April, he increased his scoring average to 9.7 point per game and 43.3% in three-point shots.  During that stretch, he had games of 32 points against [[Denver Nuggets|Denver]] and 27 points against [[Portland Trail Blazers|Portland]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Nuggets 131-126 Lakers (15 March, 2025 |url=https://www.espn.com.sg/nba/game/_/gameId/401705531/lakers-nuggets |website=ESPN Singapore |access-date=1 November 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title=Trail Blazers end season with 109-81 win over short-handed playoff-bound Lakers|agency=Associated Press
| website=ESPN | date=April 13, 2025 | url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401705765 | access-date=2025-12-07}}</ref>  For the season, Knecht shot 37.6% from three-point range and averaged 9.1 points per game.<ref name= gamelog/>

On December 15, 2025, Knecht was assigned to the [[South Bay Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Lakers' Dalton Knecht: Assigned to South Bay |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/lakers-dalton-knecht-assigned-to-south-bay/ |website=[[CBS Sports]] |access-date=December 16, 2025 |date=December 16, 2025}}</ref>
